articleTitle: Triangular ray tube analysis of dielectric lens antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The dielectric lens is a viable alternative to the reflector as the main mission antenna to provide communication satellite services in the millimetre wave band. Of the various types of dielectric lenses available, the thin spherical lens is particularly suited for satellite usage. Its advantages are many, including low weight obtained through zoning, centre feeding with no blockage, circular symmetry for ease of fabrication and wide scanning capability with minimal gain loss. In addition, surface matching by means of circumferential slots is used to reduce weight further and minimise surface reflection loss. Most of the lens analyses published in the literature e.g. [1,2], are of the scalar ray tracing type where differentiation is not made between TE and TM incidences on the lens. Also, the effects of matching layers and zoning steps are not taken into consideration. In this paper, we are presenting an analysis approach that is valid for any type of dielectric lens where surface matching and zoning steps are correctly treated and the ray tracing contains both TE and TM components. As a result, we observe very good agreement between measurements and predictions of gain patterns for both thin spherical lens and thick shaped lens.

articleTitle: A dual-polarised sar antenna based on slotted waveguide technology
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The first Canadian remote sensing satellite was launched in November 1995. The payload is a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). The SAR antenna is a 15m.∗1.5m. C-band horizontally polarised (HP) phase-scanned planar array. The scanned antenna beam can illuminate a portion of the earth's surface which is selected independently of the position of the satellite in its orbit. The beam reconfigurability property also allows alternative operational SAR modes, providing many choices of image resolution and image area.

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental studies on coupling of microwave pulses into cavities through narrow slots
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, physical model for microwave pulse coupling into cavities through narrow slots is presented, and the equation for predicting the dependence of coupling on the polarization directions of the incident pulse is derived. The modified FDTD method is used to simulate the coupling process. We observe the resonant and enhancement effects which occur in the process, and present the condition at which the resonant effect takes place. Furthermore, we validate our theoretical and numerical results experimentally.

articleTitle: Trends, system architecture, and networking issues in advanced multimedia satellite systems
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper provides a high level discussion of the trends, system architecture, and networking issues in advanced multimedia satellite systems utilizing multi-beams, Ka-band, onboard processing, and ATM-based packet switching technologies. The issues that are discussed here are based on the Advanced Satcom system which is a wideband wireless platform to complement broadband wireline technologies for delivery of interactive multimedia services to consumers and businesses across North America. The Advanced Satcom program is a government R&D initiative with participation of the Canadian space industry. The program is now being considered for implementation by Telesat as a potential owner, operator, and wholesale service provider. Launch of this system is planned for 1999 with in-service date in the year 2000.

articleTitle: Classical and modified MMDS Yagi-Uda antennas
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper classical and modified Yagi-Uda MMDS receiving antennas are analysed. Analysis and optimisation methods based on rigorous practical requirements are described. The antennas consist of half-wave dipole, 12 wire rod directors and 3 rod reflectors. Both antennas were realized. Measured and calculated results have been compared.

articleTitle: A Ka-band HBT double balanced upconvert mixer
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A Ka-band GaInP/GaAs HBT double balanced upconvert mixer has been designed and fabricated. This circuit is to be used in a multifunction T/R module for local multipoint distribution systems (LMDS) which include both analog and digital transmission. A conversion gain of 1 dB, and an output power of −10 dBm from 27 to 30 GHz for an LO input power of 10 dBm at 26 GHz were measured. The LO isolation to the output was measured to be 20 dB. These results are the best reported at Ka-band for a mixer using transistors from digital HBT library.

articleTitle: Modeling wave mechanics using lattice gas automata
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The study of wave mechanics in electromagnetism has traditionally been approached from a differential equation description of the physics. An alternative are Lattice Gas Automata, which arc discrete dynamical systems and are based on a microscopic model of the physics being simulated. A lattice gas automaton (LGA) is an extremely large regular lattice of simple interconnected cells where each cell of the lattice implements the same rule. The use of LGAs has received the most attention in the modeling of fluid dynamics, and are capable of yielding the same behavior as that described by the Navier-Stokes (NS) equation, which govern the fluid's dynamics. The use of LGAs for modeling linear wave mechanics is fairly straightforward as it is a limiting case of the more general NS equation. In this paper we discuss how lattice gas automata are used to model linear wave behavior, with specific emphasis on the added requirements for application to electromagnetism. Several obstacles, such as the ability to model material inhomogeneities and dissipation, have to be considered. More importantly, the standard LGA rules offer only scalar based descriptions. We present a method of implementing vector LGA's, thus giving a basis for modeling Maxwell's equations.

articleTitle: Indirect optically injection-locked array of phase-locked C-band oscillators
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents multiple optically injection-locked phase-controlled C-band oscillators and their application in phased array antennas. Injection-locking enables continuous phase shift while providing gain, and can be used in antenna calibration. The microwave injecting signal is delivered to the oscillators through an optical fiber link.

articleTitle: Performance enhancement of ehf cavity-backed antenna element
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Cavity-backed antennas have been used extensively in various applications in the past. The light weight, low loss and relative ease of fabrication process make them attractive candidates for high frequency applications. On the other hands, when integrated with active components their metallic walls serve as a heat sink to dissipate the heat generated by the active elements. Modification of the resonance frequency, admittance and radiation characteristics of these antennas has been achieved by the employment of unconventional cavity-backed slot antennas and adjustment of the structural features of cavity or the aperture [1].

articleTitle: Image fusion technique using fuzzy sets
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Image fusion techniques are being developed in order to generate an image which is superior to all the input images obtained by using various methods, from certainty and/or resolution points of view. These techniques have numerous applications in image processing, in general, and in biomedical imaging, in particular, where, for the same object various imaging systems produce images that have different characteristics. Fuzzy set theory can be fruitfully used for image fusion since the relation itself between tissues and pixel values is fuzzy by nature and the uncertainty associated with each imaging system can be handled easily; at the same time, the theory provides a large variety of operators for combining the available fuzzy information and is well adapted to image processing [1]. In this paper a new method for multi-modality image fusion is proposed, based on the fuzzy set theory. The relation between tissues and pixel values as well as the uncertainty resulted from noise and systematic measurement errors are defined by using appropriate fuzzy sets. The method presented is based on the computation of the possibility measures of one of these fuzzy sets with respect to the other for each tissue and each image uncertainty. The corresponding values are then processed to produce the final image instead of dealing from the beginning with similar fuzzy membership functions for all the imaging systems. A simulation is also presented to show the suitability and the performance of the method.

articleTitle: EHF System architectures for broadband indoor wireless LAN and LMCS applications
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: EHF systems architectures for a broadband indoor wireless LAN and LMCS are described in this paper. The system architectures employ millimeter wave circuitry of medium complexity for switched beam arrays at a base station and portable unit (for indoor wireless LAN) and for full duplex, asymetrical, point to multipoint transceivers (for LMCS). Further the architectures employ novel “crank wave launcher with directors” microstrip antennas (for indoor wireless LAN) and dielectric resonator antennas (for LMCS).

articleTitle: On the modelling of skin effect for multiconductor transmission lines using FDTD scheme
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The losses in Multiconductor Transmission Lines (MTL) are mainly due to two factors: the nonzero conductivity of the surrounding medium (often a good insulator) and/or the lossy nanire of the conductors (i.e. resistance). These two factors are represented by per-unit-length conductance, G, and per-unit-length resistance, R, respectively. Hence, the MTL equations can be written using G, R, L (per-unit-length inductance), and C (per-unit-length capacitance).

articleTitle: Dual-band, dual-polarized microstrip arrays for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The next generation of civilian, satellite based synthetic aperture radar is expected to be multispectral with polarization synthesis, cross polarization and multi-mode capabilities. In order to minimize the overall size of the antenna subsystems required by these radars, techniques are being investigated which will allow the aperture to be shared between the multiple frequency bands and multiple polarization channels.

articleTitle: RF techniques for measuring antenna repair chemical processes
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Sacramento Air Logistics Center (SM-ALC), located at McClellan AFB, California, has been involved in the repair of military high-frequency antennas and radomes for many years. With the acquisition of precision microwave equipment in the last five years, the ALC has developed innovative methods of gauging its antenna/radome material repair processes. This paper will focus on the work done on a LS-band phased array satellite ground station antenna. Specific processes examined will be radome paint selection, phased-array receive element cleaning, and radome bonding. The history of the problems that required the repairs will be discussed. Chemical repair processes and RF test methods will be described. Manufacturer specification will be examined where available. Included in this paper will be RF test data and data analysis.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of printed meander antennas
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Meander type antennas have low-profile and are generally smaller than conventional dipoles. In this paper the effect of changing the parameters of a meander dipole on its radiation characteristics is investigated using the FDTD technique. For the antenna without any substrate, it is observed that the E and H-plane patterns are similar to a straight dipole. The gain is larger than that of a straight dipole of the same length. However, gain decreases when the antenna length exceeds about 0.6Λ. The cross-polarization increases with the increase in antenna length for a constant number of meanders. For a constant length when the number of meanders is reduced, the cross-polarization increases. For a meander dipole printed on a dielectric substrate (∊<inf>r</inf> = 10.2), the H-plane pattern is uniform for an antenna of length L = 0.25Λ, whereas, the pattern is nonuniform (< 2.0 dB) for an antenna of length L = 0.50Λ.

articleTitle: Receiving or transmitting high efficiency antenna of dual polarized printed radiating sources coupled with two waveguides
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: X band is useful to single out surface scattering especially if there is also a trend in having polarimetric S.A.R., which allows us the simultaneous acquisition of four images using receiving and transmitting antennas of dual polarizations. Polarimetric radars require the use of a double polarisations antennas having a high polarization purity and a good efficiency.

articleTitle: A mesfet balanced distributed preamplifier MMIC
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A MMIC balanced preamplifier was fabricated using a 0.8 μm gate length process. A 45 dBΩ transimpedance gain, a 6 GHz bandwidth, a 10ρA/√Hz input noise and a 12 dB CMRR were measured.

articleTitle: A slotted waveguide antenna for grain drying
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Convection drying using fossil fuel combustion is the most widely used method for drying freshly harvested grains to safe storage levels. When hot air is used to dry grains, a slow conduction heat transfer takes place from the grain surface towards the inside. The outer layers of the kernel arc dried first and become less permeable, creating case hardening (Fanslow et al., 1971). The mass transfer of the moisture however, goes from the inside of the kernel to the suface and is slowed down by the counter current heat transfer. Microwave energy can be used to dry grains in a volumetric process and thus eliminate the use of fossil fuels in regions where hydro power is available (Raghavan et al., 1993). When microwaves are used to dry grams, both heat and mass transfer are instantaneous and emerge out of the kernel. Researchers have studied the drying behavior of particulate food materials in a microwave field (Hall. 1963; Fanslow and Saul, 1971; Bhartia et al., 1973; Shivhare et al., 1991). Slotted waveguides have been successfully used to couple electromagnetic energy to materials for heating and drying purposes (Rueggeberg, 1980; Metaxas and Meredith. 1983) and for plasma applications (Ji and Gerling, 1988; Sauvé et al., 1993). The present study was aimed at determining the optimal operating parameters of a slotted waveguide applicator for continuous flow grain drying.

articleTitle: Conception d'un mÉlangeur a fet utilisant une configuration simple et balancÉe
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Résumé On propose dans cet article la conception de mélangeurs à grille utilisant une configuration simple et balancé. La configuration balancé proposée utilise un hybride en anneau dont la largeur de bande a été améliorée. La simulation des deux mélangeurs a donné un bon fonctionnement pour un signal RF et LO respectivement de 15 GHz et 13.3 GHz. Un gain de conversion allant jusqu'à 4 dB a été obtenu ainsi que des isolation IF/RF et IF/LO atteignant respectivement −56 dB et −58 dB.

articleTitle: Simulation of electromagnetic fields inside the human body using the finite integration technique
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: We investigate the penetration of electromagnetic fields caused by a cellular phone into a human head using the Finite Integration Technique in time-domain. The applied human head model is created directly from NMR data and consists of 500 000, respectively 4 million mesh cells. The final calculation domain is set up by 1.8 million cells, corresponding to 10.8 million unknowns for the electrical field and magnetic flux. With a broadband stimulation of the monopol antenna we calculate the frequency response inside the human eye over a frequency range of 300MHz up to 1.8GHz considering the dispersion of the biological tissues. Finally the farfield pattern of a hand-held device placed in the vicinity of the human head are investigated.

articleTitle: Large-scale production of X-Band power mmics for insertion in a weather radar system
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Modular Avionics Radar system produced at Northrop Grumman ESSD is an important improvement in aircraft windsheur detection capability. The system features a solid state X-Band power transmitter whose fundamental building block is a 4W GaAs MMIC. 160W transmitter output power is achieved by integrating 88 MMICs in higher level assemblies. To meet MODAR production needs, over 28,000 of these MMICs have been produced to date. Statistics-based techniques used to achieve a steady cost reduction for these MMICs are discussed.

articleTitle: An etched antenna for autoclaveable RFID tags
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The smart structures community has become interested in embedding of antennae into carbon-epoxy composite materials to facilitate the delivery of power to an embedded sensor system as well as transfer of data and instructions to and from the sensor system. Once a sensor is attached to this embedded antenna, the resultant sensor system can be used to measure, for example, temperature, strain, acceleration, or chemical processes, and thus be used to monitor the “health” of the structure, the state of cure of the part, or perhaps external stimuli.

articleTitle: Effects of finite ground plane and substrate dimensions on the radiation pattern of a circular microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip antennas have became one of the most popular antenna types and in the past twenty years they have been analysed extensively. However, most of the computations are based on the assumption of infinite fiat ground planes. In the past decade, some research have been done to investigate the effect of finite ground planes on the performance of microstrip antennas [1][2]. Some of these studies have been done in two dimensions, assuming an infinite ground plane in one dimension. In the present work, the method of moment for bodies of revolution, a powerful numerical method, has been used. The three dimensional solution is simplified by using the symmetry about the azimuthal axis [2].

articleTitle: Efficient electrical parameters extraction methods for modeling crosstalk and radiated emission from PCBs
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Several efficient techniques to reduce the computational cost and memory storage requirements for the calculation of the electrical parameters of 3-D structures are presented in [1]. In this paper, the electrical parameters are employed in the calculation of crosstalk and radiated emissions from traces on printed circuit boards (PCBs). The inclusion of these aspects are very important in the analysis and design of electromagnetically compatible products.

articleTitle: The TLM based FD-TD modelling with PML absorbing boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The transmission-line-matrix (TLM) based finite-difference time-domain (FD-TD) has been introduced and generalized recently. The method is equivalent to the 3D TLM symmetrical condensed node but is computed directly in terms of field quantities in a FD-TD fashion. In this paper, the implementation of recently developed PML absorbing boundary conditions in the TLM based FD-TD grid is presented. Numerical results show that PML is effective and efficient in absorbing both the evanescent and propagating modes in a three dimensional TLM-based grid.

articleTitle: Analysis of 3D planar structures by TLM cuboid condensed node
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the application of the transmission line matrix (TLM) method to numerical analysis of 3D planar structures by means of the 3D cuboid condensed node with cells of arbitrary aspect ratio. An air bridge and a rectangular spiral inductor are analyzed with the TLM cuboid scheme, and the results are compared with those obtained by measurement, the spectral domain approach and traditional stub-loaded TLM. The comparison clearly indicates that the cuboid cell yields results close to the reference data than the stub-loaded scheme.

articleTitle: Okoshi's planar method corrected for accurate analysis of high Q patch resonators
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: To analyze high Q circuits, we need a very accurate method. Traditional methods, such as 2D planar circuit, Modal or Okoshi's, 3-D methods, moment or variational methods, are not versatile or accurate enough for these circuits. In this paper, a better method, the combined 2D plus variational method together with reciprocity and zero tangential field, will be presented to analyze microstrip patches.

articleTitle: Characterisation of passive functional elements for microwave monolithic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The modeling and characterisation of five types of passive functional elements, namely Metal-Isolator-Metal (MIM) capacitors, interdigital capacitors and octogonal inductors for microstrip technology and two CPW discontinuities (open-end and short-end stub) for coplanar technology are presented. Analytical formulas easy to use in CAD are proposed to calculate the dominant passive elements of these models. Good agreement between these results and measurements performed in the frequency range 1–30 GHz has been observed.

articleTitle: Method of evaluation of radiation fields in Fresnel region for circular and elliptic aperture antennas
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A method of evaluating Fresnel zone radiation fields is studied for circular and elliptic aperture antennas which is illumated with an arbitrary aperture distributions. Fresnel zone field is represented by a series of generalized Lommel functions of two parameters defined here. It is shown that the generalized Lommel functions with any degrees and orders may be derived from the original Lommel functions <sup>[1]</sup> using the recurrence relations. The validity of the expressions is verified numerically by comparing with those obtained from the method by Sun and Rusch <sup>[2]</sup> and from direct numerical integrations. This method may also be applied to predict the far field pattern of offset typed parabolic reflector antennas <sup>[3]</sup>. The three dimensional pictures of Fresnel patterns for circular apterute with tapered illumination as well as uniform distribution are obtained.

articleTitle: Computations and measurements of radiation from printed circuit boards
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Results of computation and measurement of radiated emissions of high speed digital circuits on printed circuit boards are presented. Computations involve a complete frequency domain analysis of the circuit. From a knowledge of the voltages and currents at discontinuities, the current distribution on the printed tracks is evaluated. Emission levels are subsequently computed using the current distribution.

articleTitle: Internal electromagnetic scattering of an open cylinder with complex terminations
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper deals with the internal scattering of an open cylinder that is illuminated by an incident plane wave. Three different types of terminations for the cylinder are considered: a short-circuit flat plate, a plug represented by a section of coaxial guide with a short-circuit plate, and a set of coplanar blades. In the last termination, energy transmitted through the gaps in the blades is absorbed by a load. Of interest is the monostatic radar cross-section (RCS) of the cylinder with these terminations. In the case of the blades, the spectral energy of the scattered wave which is modulated by blade rotation, is also evaluated.

articleTitle: Slot mutual coupling effects in multimode microwave applicators
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Slotted waveguide arrays have been widely used as radiators of electromagnetic energy in industrial applicators. The theory of radiating slots cut in the broad wall of a standard rectangular waveguide has been developed extensively in the literature [1]-[2].

articleTitle: A novel microstrip-fed multi-segment dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper investigates a novel multi-segment dielectric resonator antenna (DRA). The antenna consists of a thin segments of different permittivity material bonded to the underside of a rectangular dielectric resonator segment. The multi-segment DRA element is excited by a microstrip line. The permittivity and thickness of the segments are used to concentrate the fields of the micro-scrip line and enhance the coupling from the line to the dielectric resonator segment. Experimental results are presented on a two-segment DRA consisting of a thin segment of high permittivity bonded to a dielectric resonator segment of low permittivity. Without the high permittivity segment, coupling from the microstrip line to the DRA is quite weak, achieving a return loss of only 5 dB. With the high permittivity segment, a maximum return loss of 24 dB was achieved with a 10 dB return loss bandwidth of 17%.

articleTitle: Modified spatial decomposition technique for solution of large electromagnetic scattering problems
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Using the Method of Moments (MoM)[1] for the scattering by electrically large bodies results in large matrices which dictate excessive computer storage and execution time. The Spatial Decomposition Technique (SDT)[2] was proposed to circumvent high demand on the computer resources and also reduce numerical difficulties. It divides the scatterer into an arbitrary number of N distinct spatial subzones. At the virtual interface separating the two subzones, the tangential virtual currents on one side of the interface must be equal, but opposite to the tangential virtual currents on the other side of the interface. The excitation for every subzone consists of the original incident plane wave and additional excitation due to the electric currents residing on the surfaces on the remaining spatial subzones. The initial current distribution may be approximated by either the physical optics or another method. The iterative process begins from the first subzone and then shifts to the next adjacent subzone, and so forth. The number of iterations will depend on the accuracy desired. During the implementation, the currents in subzones are updated and the latest surface currents as the excitation for the subzone of interest are always used.

articleTitle: Slot antenna on perfectly conducting spheroid coated with homogeneous materials
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Slot antennas on dielectric-coated perfectly conducting objects have extensively been studied by many investigators. For these problems, exact analytic solutions are available only for a limited number of geometries. These geometries include circular and elliptic cylinders, as well as, spheres and spheroids. Since these solutions maintain mathematical rigor, they provide not only exact solutions for their respective geometries, but also the evaluation of approximate and numerical solutions. The slot antennas on a dielectric-coated sphere and circular cylinder have been investigated by Shafai[1], Lin[2] and other authors. Slot antennas on a coated spheroid, on the other hand, have been discused by Wait [3] and Weeks[4], but their discussions are only for the rotationally symmetric slots. A more general case, the nonsymmetric slots, have not been studied extensively, and, it is the subject of this paper.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka-Band hybrid transistor dielectric resonator oscillator
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A design procedure for a Ka-Band PHEMT dielectric resonator oscillator (DRO) is given. A linear design approach is used to realize the 28.5 GHz oscillator in a hybrid MMIC/MIC format.

articleTitle: Lens antenna with improved efficiency for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The rapid growth of spectral utilization has necessitated the progress toward higher frequency bands to resolve the spectral crowding problem. However, before the successful transition to higher frequency bands can be realized, critical components and appropriate tools such as propagation modelling need to be developed. In the millimeter-wave band, many of these technologies have progressed rapidly in the last decade. Several millimeter-wave systems including satellite, mobile and personal communications as well as various commercial and scientific applications have been proposed. Antennas are one of the key components for the successful operation of these systems.

articleTitle: Low loss wideband patch antenna for EHF indoor systems
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The design procedure for a low-loss wideband microstrip patch antenna to be used as the key element for an indoor phased array is adressed. For these indoor communications systems, wideband elements are required to support multimedia transmission and to minimize the requirements for external circuitry. A microstrip patch with stacked structures has been developed using the FDTD method and the results obtained are compared to those given by a commercial software package (Ensemble). The FDTD method is used to calculate the radioelectric characteristics (input impedance, S parameters, etc…) of the modeled antenna. This method can be applied to problem exhibiting a complex structure which otherwise may be very difficult to solve using other analytical or numerical methods. Also, it is a time domain method by which transient phenomena can be studied. Finally, the Fourier transform of the FDTD transient results gives frequency domain results over a wide spectrum. A development which leads to an impedance bandwidth over 13% and a minimum gain of 8 dB will be presented and discussed in view of the system requierements.

articleTitle: Wide band stripline dipole arrays
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The development of a very wideband balanced stripline printed dipole array placed above a conducting ground plane, as shown in Fig. 1, is discussed in this paper. A balanced printed dipole has its arms printed on the top and bottom conducting plane of a thin substrate mounted normal to the array ground plane. An integrated matching network forms the centre conductor of the stripline feed. The arms of the dipole are bifurcated with one branch parallel to ground and the other branch tilted at an angle. For the dipole considered here, the arms are at 45°. The dipole is top loaded by a parasitic element as shown in Fig. 2. This form of the dipole is found, both theoretically and experimentally, to possess broadband pattern and input impedance properties even under wide scan conditions.

articleTitle: A powerful EM analysis tool based on the FD-TD simulation method
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Packaging and interconnects not only impact the functional characteristics (the ability and speed with which a given inpnt signal may be modified to some desired and appropriate output signal) of a product, but also how the product performs in any number of applications. These applications can range from military and automotive environments where mechanical integrity must be maintained as well as an ability to operate over a wide margin of temperature extremes. In power distribution appliactions impedance must be kept to a minimum; board layout and packaging have a significant impact in the impedance levels. Further, higher power densities, found in circuits which have increasing device and board densities, must be managed to prevent system failure.

articleTitle: Efficient and flexible electromagnetic simulation for planar and 3D structures
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Electromagnetic simulation tools have been getting a great deal of attention in the electronic design industry because of their accuracy, capability and flexibility. In this paper, we would like to discuss the improvement on the efficient and flexible electromagnetic simulation tool — the IE3D Electromagnetic Simulation and Optimization Package.

articleTitle: Development of a 20 GHz to baseband MMIC direct downconverter for advanced SATCOM terminal applications
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) 20 GHz / baseband downconverter has been developed for implementation in a low cost EHF SATCOM terminal. This paper reports on the development aspects of the mixer and the PHEMT diode model. The mixer conversion loss was measured to be 9.6dB ± 0.4dB over the 50 MHz to 450 MHz IF frequency range. The 1dB compression point was 10dBm and the two-tone. 3rd order IM intercept point was 20dBm. The single sideband (SSB) noise figure was about 10.5dB between 50 MHz and 450 MHz and the RF/LO isolation was 26dB. Measured and predicted performances showed good agreement.

articleTitle: RCS of metallic plates with apertures
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper investigates the radar cross-section (RCS) of metallic plates with square or rectangular apertures. We determine the RCS of such metallic plates by using software based on the moment-method solution of the electric field integral equation (EFIE), and also using the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD). The RCS is computed as a function of the number, the size, and the shape of apertures, as well as the thickness of the plate. We compare the computed results with measurements made in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Analysis of inhomogeneous dielectric resonator structures using fem and CFH
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes an efficient method for the analysis of cylindrical cavity resonator structures with inhomogeneous dielectric medium. In this approach, the field equations are formulated using the Laplace-domain finite element method and are solved using the complex frequency hoppoing (CFH) technique. CFH is a moment matching technique which has been used successfully in the circuit simulation area for solution of large set of ordinary differential equations. The proposed technique is faster than the conventional approach by one to three orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: The FD-TD formulation of the 3D TLM symmetrical condensed node and its applications
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the finite-difference time-domain (FD-TD) formulation of the 3D transmission-line-matrix (TLM) symmetrical condensed node is presented. It allows a direct use of field quantities and therefore the applications of modelling tools and techniques developed for the conventional TD-TD method. Numerical results are given for modelling general electromagnetic media including anisotropic, dispersive and nonlinear media.

articleTitle: Corner reflector antenna fed by slotted cylinder
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation pattern of a corner reflector fed by a circular conducting cylinder with an axial slot is examined. An integral equation for the TE case is derived using Green's second identity. The method of moments is then employed to obtain a numerical solution for the integral equation. In order to study the effect of the slotted cylinder feed, radiation patterns corresponding to a line source feed are also calculated. The comparison between radiation patterns of corner reflector antenna fed by a line source and their correspondence with a slotted circular cylinder feed showed that the later can give a narrower beam width, which increases the antenna gain.

articleTitle: Future satellite communications at the European space agency
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Since the early 70's, the European Space Agency, ESA, has pioneered fixed and mobile communication satellite developments for European regional applications. It has also contributed to the creation and expansion in Europe of a competitive telecommunication satellite industry.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic levitation using the fringing fields of a microwave cavity
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Levitation of a rotor within an electrostatically driven micromotor has been proposed as a method of overcoming the relatively large frictional resistance caused by contact friction. A novel arrangement in which the rotor is levitated by embedding it within the fringing fields of a pair of microwave cavities is described. The nature of the levitating system is a dynamic one, and requires no feedback as all movements by the levitated element are self correcting until equilibrium is achieved. Although this means the system is relatively simple, it also means that analysis of the levitation process is complex, and stability predictions are problematic. For this reason, as well as experimental analysis of the system, a simulation of the cavity geometry using an EM finite element modelling package (HFSS) is used. HFSS allows analysis of the levitating fields, and gives a thorough understanding of the fields and energies generated and optimum equilibrium conditions. Two re-entrant cavities have been modelled using the package, and the element to be levitated has been added. Energies and field strengths have been calculated and optimum component dimensions selected. The experimental setup is outlined, along with the equivalent geometry generated in HFSS, and results obtained from both approaches are discussed.

articleTitle: A software tool for electromagnetic environment modelling
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A user-friendly software tool for electromagnetic environment modelling (STEEM) has been developed to provide designers with the data needed to properly shield systems against electromagnetic interference (EMI). Two computational engines are included, one based on analytic expressions of radiated fields, and the other based on a ray tracing algorithm using the uniform theory of diffraction. STEEM is equipped with an AutoCAD interface, making it an easy-to-use, flexible and powerful environment modelling package.

articleTitle: Expressions for the field line equations in potential fields
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Construction of field lines for vector fields can be performed by a variety of analytical or graphical methods. Except for a small number of simple geometries, where closed analytical expressions can be obtained, the shape of the field lines is determined by numerical computation or evaluated approximately by physical modelling techniques [1]. In this paper, we consider irrotational vector fields that are derived from scalar potential functions and expansions are obtained for the field line equations valid in the neighbourhood of any point at which the potential and its derivatives are defined.

articleTitle: Antenna payload design for advanced satcom satellites
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Advanced Satcom Satellites require uplink (30 GHz) and downlink (20 GHz) antennas providing regional earth coverage (Canada, CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico) using high gain multiple overlapping spot beams. The antenna coverage with 128 beams that are arranged in a hexagonal grid fashion is shown in Figure 1. Critical antenna design parameters required for this system are very low scan loss over a ±9 beamwidths scan, maximum coverage area gain and moderate sidelobe isolation among alternate beams that reuse the frequency. In order to satisfy these requirements, a dielectric spherical lens antenna has been selected for both Tx and Rx antennas to take advantage of its excellent scan capabilities and its centre-feeding configuration. The radiation characteristics of the beams produced by such a lens using septet feed per beam on Rx and single feed per beam on Tx have been optimized and are presented here. The resultant beams show scan loss of less than 0.4 dB over the coverage region and meet the system requirements.

articleTitle: Generalization of the Ludwig-3 Definition for linear co-polarization and cross-polarization
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the generalization of the Ludwig-3 definition of linear co-polarization and cross-polarization. We say that our definition is a generalization because our definition agrees with the Ludwig-3 definition on boresight but departs further from the Ludwig-3 definition as the observation angle θ departs from zero as a result of the presence of a cos(θ) term in the generalized definition. The generalized definition assigns the linear co-polarized component at an arbitrary point on the observation sphere to be the electric field vector whose projection onto the aperture plane is oriented in the direction of a perfectly linearly polarized aperture field. The linear cross-polarized component at the same arbitrary point on the observation sphere is then the electric field vector orthogonal to the co-polarized component in the propagation plane. Since the Ludwig-3 definition does not take into account the additional rotation incurred by the presence of the cos(θ) term. a perfectly linearly polarized field in the aperture results in a zero cross-polarization at the observation point by the generalized definition, but not so in general by the Ludwig-3 definition. The discrepancy between the two definitions becomes significant for a general observation direction when θ > 15°, with the largest discrepancy being found for φ = 45°.

articleTitle: Design of a low-cost MIC antenna array network at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This project deals with the design and the realization of a low-cost MIC antenna array subsystem at an operating frequency of 9.71 GHz. Applications for this kind of antenna are found in indoor wireless communications systems. Low power radar is also a potential field of application. We present a proposed topology to perform beam switching in many azimuthal directions and in two elevations. Elevation switching is implemented by reflection phase shifters in a phased array, with the constraint of a constant module in both phase states. Loaded line phase shifters are also implemented. Finally, antenna performances are showed and discussed.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of a small, low cost ancchoic chamber at memorial university of newfoundland
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: C-CORE's newly built anechoic chamber provides the only controlled environment in Newfoundland in which to conduct microwave measurements with minimal electromagnetic interference. The measurement of reflectivity levels from the chamber surfaces and of radiation patterns were used to evaluate the chamber. Sample measurements of the free space voltage standing wave ratio technique indicated that the worst reflectivity level was −18.8 dB at 2.1 GHz. Comparison of antenna radiation patterns, previously measured using compact range methods in the University of Manitoba's anechoic chamber, with those measured in C-CORE's anechoic chamber shows a very good agreement.

articleTitle: Investigation of geometrically small features within numerical solutions to electromagnetic field problems
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper we consider the numerical solution of electromagnetic field problems involving geometrically small features. The numerical approaches considered are the three dimensional symmetric condensed node transmission line matrix (TLM) method, the Yee finite-difference time-domain (FD-TD) method, and lattice gas automata (LGA). The problems were selected to allow for rigorous computational investigation, and consist of perfectly conducting cavities and thin dielectric layers. The cavity results indicate the dominant error with TLM and FD-TD methods is dispersion, while dissipation is the dominant error with LGA. The ‘cursed-fin’ analysis indicates an initial estimate of the LGA to TLM (or FD-TD) mesh spacing ratio is in the range of 10:1 to 30:1. Stair-stepping errors are minimal in LGA analysis of curved conducting surfaces due to the extremely fine spatial discritization required. The accuracy of LGA and TLM approaches to the modelling of thin dielectric regions, such as the skin of a biological model, was tested through analysis of a Gaussian pulsed plane wave normally incident on a thin dielectric layer. Numerical results were compared to an analytic solution.

articleTitle: Generalized scattering matrix and symmetry principles for infinite planar structures
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a technique for determining the scattering coefficients of the Generalized Scattering Matrix (GSM) for an infinite planar structure whose operation is prescribed. The technique is partly a synthesis tool in that it allows to identify some geometrical properties of the structure from the relationships between various coefficients of the GSM. These relationships are cast into a formalism that simplifies and generalizes the development of many previously reported results. We also apply the technique to various structures for the purpose of demonstrating its use and validity. When this technique is applied to Linear or circular polarizers with the GSM incorporating only the dominant mode, we find that ideal polarizers are possible only at normal incidence, regardless of their specific physical realizations. Similarly, we find that a structure corresponding to the reciprocal circular polarization selective surface must satisfy the property of 2-fold rotational symmetry, except in a limited neighborhood of the normal incidence where the property of reciprocity suffices, and must not satisfy the property of longitudinal reflection symmetry.

articleTitle: Comparison of magnetically induced elf fields in humans computed by FDTD and scalar potential FD codes
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of the magnetically induced low frequency electric and current density fields within an anatomically realistic model of the full human body, as computed using two different numerical techniques. The first method is a full wave quasi-static finite-difference time-domain method. The second method is based on a representation of the first-order internal electric field in terms of a scalar conduction potential plus a vector potential for the lowest-order applied magnetic field. Each code was used to calculate the fields, induced by three orthogonal uniform magnetic fields, in a 7.2 mm-resolution human full-body model. Three-dimensional correlation coefficients of better than 99.8% were observed between results computed by the two methods. Individual edge electric fields typically agree to 3 significant digits.

articleTitle: A 30 GHz regenerative divide-by-2 frequency divider
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: There is presently a drive towards the consumer use of Ka-band satellite systems to extend the information highway to areas unserviced by the terrestrial infrastructure. In order for these systems to be commercially successful, there is a need for low cost user terminals. Microwave frequency digital prescalers/dividers are commercially available to about 15 GHz. To perform frequency division above 15 GHz, analog techniques must be used. This paper describes the design and development of a 30 GHz divide-by-2 regenerative type divider, also known as a Miller divider [1], for use in a Ka-band synthesizer. It will form part of the PLL chain of the synthesizer. The divider follows the output of a Ka-band VCO, so that once the signal is divided in half, commercially available chip type dividers/prescalers and components can be used for the rest of the PLL chain. The design approach, component selection, fabrication and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Explicit upwind difference schemes for lossy multiconductor transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Written in a conservation law form, the time domain multiconductor transmission line (MTL) equations are solved by splitting the fluxes and using a second order accurate upwind differencing technique. The solutions of the initial and boundary value problems are compared to those obtained by employing the standard finite difference time domain (FDTD) scheme based on the Yee version of the leap-frog method. For any general explicit numerical scheme, for a given MTL, only the fastest propagating mode can be solved for at the Courant number of the scheme. This causes the other slower modes to disperse. The results of our comparisons, show that the upwind scheme produces much less numerical dispersion for the slower propagating modes than the standard FDTD scheme. In addition, the Courant number of the second order upwind scheme is twice of that of the investigated FDTD schemes. These advantages make the second order upwind scheme a better tool to model any MTL with linear terminations.

articleTitle: Two loaded wire antennas above a Half-Space with a cover layer
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Two identical straight thin-wire antennas are located in free space, above a plane-stratified dielectric consisting of a continuously layered dielectric slab covering a homogeneous dielectric half-space (See Fig.1). One of the antennas is excited by a pulsed voltage source ν<inf>A</inf>(t), while the other one is used as a receiving antenna to measure the total current induced on its surface. Part of that current is due to the electromagnetic fields reflected by the inhomogeneous half-space, and is therefore influenced by the material properties of that half-space. Therefore, analyzing this configuration may be of use in inverse-scattering applications such as ground radar.

articleTitle: High resolution ultra wideband arrays
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Highly thinned or sparsely filled arrays can reduce the quantity of electronics supporting the array and the data-handling requirements of a high resolution imaging system for a fixed number of array channels, greatly enlarge the aperture, and correspondingly improve its resolving power. It is well-known that the cost is a dramatic decrease in dynamic range, or contrast. Aperture thinning generally leaves the shapes of the main lobe and near-in sidelobes intact, but the loss in absolute gain implies that main lobe energy has been redistributed into the side radiation region. In conventional narrowband arrays, periodic thinning produces grating lobes of similar shape and strength to the main lobe. Aperiodic thinning destroys the coherent sidelobe buildup in the grating lobes but not the grating lobe energy, which becomes distributed throughout the visible region in a manner determined by the particular thinning procedure. It is common knowledge that sidelobe statistics are similar for a wide variety of thinning procedures, both deterministic and random, with a few notable exceptions [1]. Thus many proposed designs for high resolution two-dimensional arrays are based upon a random distribution of elements [2].

articleTitle: Integration aspects of a 29.5 GHz MMIC single sideband modulator
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Direct modulation is proposed for future Ka-band communications systems to reduce the cost and size, and to improve the reliability. The RF circuitry can potentially be integrated onto a single wafer using advanced GaAs-based PHEMT MMIC technology. In this paper, the performance of a baseband to 29.15 GHz single-halanced mixer is reported. Also, the integration aspects of a baseband to 29.5 GHz single sideband (SSB) modulator for advanced satcom terminals is discussed.

articleTitle: Estimates of electromagnetic compatibility requirements in health care environments
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The characteristics of electromagnetic (E.M.) fields due to portable/mobile radio-frequency (R.F.) sources inside buildings are examined with particular attention to health care environments snch as in hospital rooms. Attention is given in particular to the identification of high field levels which might exceed proposed susceptibility thresholds for medical electronic equipment. Effects of the room geometry, surface material properties and R.F. source location are examined, using geometric-optics ray modelling along with the image technique. It is found that the interference patterns generated can exhibit field levels substantially above simplistic free-space estimates. The magnitude and distribution of such high field conditions are increasingly serious with the occurances of multiple high conductivity reflective surfaces.

articleTitle: System considerations for active SAR antennae
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A proposed baseline space-borne Advanced SAR active array concept is a dual-frequency (L and C bands), dual polarization, planar array, with 1920 C-Band T/R modules and 240 L-Band T/R modules, distributed behind the radiating aperture. It comprises five panels, each one approximately 4m in elevation by 3.2m in azimuth, for a total antenna aperture size of 4m × 16.0m. Each panel is subdivided into 8 tiles, distributed 4 in elevation by 2 in azimuth. Each tile is thus approximately 1m × 1.6m. The mass of this design is estimated at close to 1700kg, which is almost twice the corresponding Radarsat mass. This paper looks into a possible reformulation of the system level requirements which greatly simplifies the antenna design, thus decreasing mass and cost.

articleTitle: Microwave dielectric resonator tuning with two-varactor circuit
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The coupling between a TE<inf>01δ</inf> cylindrical dielectric resonator and two microstnp lines loaded with two varactor diodes is modeled by a lumped equivalent circuit. The range of electronic tuning of the resonant frequency is determined as a function of the electromagnetic parameters of the structure.

articleTitle: An object-oriented approach to the transmission line matrix method
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) method, firstly developed by Johns and Beurle [1], is a numerical technique for solving electromagnetic scattering problems based on a discretization of Huygen's model of wave propagation. This method employs a Cartesian mesh of transmission lines to discretize the original problem's domain and simulates propagation of delta function electromagnetic impulses in space through propagation of voltage and current delta functions in the transmission line grid. Firstly conceived for free-space two-dimensional homogeneous problems, the method was soon extended to three dimensions [2] and to take into account dielectric loading and losses [3-4]. A comprehensive bibliography on the TLM method as well as a description of its evolution can be found in [5].

articleTitle: Spectral domain analysis of quasi-planar transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The spectral domain approach is extended in order to take into account effects of mounting grooves, finite metallization thickness, substrate anisotropy and multilayer media, To demonstrate the versatility and accuracy of the extended technique, computed propagation characteristics are presented for several representative examples, and compared with available experimental data and results by other numerical methods. These examples include chanuelized coplanar waveguides, groove mounted and pedestal supported suspended striplines, ferrite-loaded finlines, and inset dielectric guides.

articleTitle: Measured and computed results of air-to-ground communication performance of 2 aircraft at VHF/UHF frequencies
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Method of Moments is often used to simulate the radiation patterns of aircraft antennas. The assessment of antenna performance in terms of radiation pattern information alone is difficult, because the overall effect of the pattern on communications performance during typical flight profiles is unclear. We present a numerical methodology to combine the three-dimensional radiation patterns with standard propagation models and evaluate the resulting communications over a realistic flight profile. Numerical grid models radiation patterns are first validated against scale model measured radiation patterns, and thereafter predicted received signal strength iscompared to measured signals during a flight trial. The mean difference in predicted and measured signal strength is 2.8 dB for the transport aircraft trial and 3.46 dB for the trainer aircraft trial using flight profiles with distances ranging between 0 to 70 nautical miles (nmi) and altitudes ranging from 300 ft to 10000 ft. The method allows antenna placement studies to be conducted with more useful results.

articleTitle: Mode tuning of circular cylindrical microwave cavity loaded by lossy dielectric slab
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A circular cylindrical metallic cavity loaded with homogeneous lossy dielectric slab is analysed. The mode tuning effects of loaded cavity are investigated, wherein the effect of the losses is introduced through the complex values of the dielectric constant and the frequency. The characteristic equation is obtained using the transverse resonance method. The complex resonant frequencies are determined by numerically solving this transcendental equation. The resonant frequencies and the damping factor curves versus filling factor of microwave cavity are shown.

articleTitle: De-embedding MICs/MMICs in fixed-length fixtures: Use of symmetric two-port transmission-line discontinuities
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new technique is developed, which is particularly useful for de-embedding MICs/MMICs in fixed-length fixtures. The use of symmetric two-port transmission-line discontinuities at the reference plane and at an offset location is an important feature. The scattering parameters of the discontinuities are obtained as a by-product. The associated theory is supported by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Dual band dual polarized radiating element development
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: For the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) applications antenna candidates with dual-polarized dual-band capability are investigated. The microstrip technology is considered and several antenna configurations are selected, analyzed, designed and evaluated. Here, three different candidates are presented that use different combinations of substrates and antenna geometries. Their performance is briefly reviewed and compared.

articleTitle: Modeling a chain of biological cells in an ELF electric field
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: External electromagnetic fields can interact with biological cells in several ways, including modifying transmembrane potential. For a simplified spherical model of a single cell in a uniform electric field, a closed form expression for transmembrane potential has been obtained. For environmental fields, the field induced transmembrane potential is negligibly small.

articleTitle: 0.5W and 1.5W Ka-band PHEMT power MMICs for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Described are the design, fabrication and measured results of a pair of PHEMT power MMIC chip sets, one operating at 31GHz and the other operating at 35GHz. Each chip set contains a high gain 0.5W driver and a 1.5W power MMIC. The demonstrated high yield and low cost of these MMICs makes them attractive building blocks for today's millimeter-wave systems.

articleTitle: Radarsat sar antenna in-flight pattern measurements
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Canadian Radarsat satellite was launched on November 4, 1995 and is now in routine operation. Radarsat's payload consists of a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging instrstrument, and it is the first operational satellite SAR with an antenna which can reconfigure its elevation beam electronically. The SAR Antenna is a large deployable slotted waveguide planar array (1.5m by 15m) operating at 5.3 GHz. The antenna comprises 32 slotted waveguide rows with electronic Variable Phase Shifters which are set to produce various pseudo-trapezoidal elevation beam shapes. These beams vary in elevation width from 1.6° to 11.3° and scan over elevation angles from −21° (min. near edge) to +20° (max. far edge) relative to the antenna boresight. This provides ground coverage anywhere within an accessibility strip of width greater than 500 km. The along track (azimuth plane) radiation pattern is a pencil beam. In order to achieve optimum performance, accurate beam pattern information must be used in the processing. Unlike preceding satellite SAR systems, Radarsat operates with many different beams, and so the beam characterisation is a major task. This paper describes the procedures that were used to predict the patterns before launch and to measure them in-flight, and presents results demonstrating good correspondence between the two sets of data.

articleTitle: Effects of horizontal linear section of a curl antenna on radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A curl antenna fed from a coaxial line has been proposed as a radiation element of circular polarization [1]. The curl antenna consists of vertical, horizontal linear sections, and a curled section. This paper presents the effects of the horizontal linear section on the radiation characteristics. The radiation characteristics for higher-order operation modes [2] of the curl antenna are also discussed.

articleTitle: Overview of Japanese communication satellites
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Communication satellite technologies in Japan have been developed by NASDA in collaboration with other agencies since the first communication satellite CS and the first broadcasting satellite BS were operated. Currently, several commercial communication satellites are in operation and various advanced communication experiments are planned with use of new engineering test satellites. In this paper, some operational and planned Japanese communication satellites, together with an overview of their development.

articleTitle: Direct radiating array for meo communication satellite
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A common but difficult antenna requirement for medium earth orbit (MEO) communication satellite is the generation of simultaneous multiple beams over a wide coverage area. The beams should be highly overlapped in order to provide high coverage gain but yet with sufficient decay in the sidelobes to yield the necessary isolation between every other beam. An efficient antenna solution to this problem for MEOs operating at S- or L-band is the use of a direct radiating array (DRA) fed by a low signal level multiple beam forming network (BFN). Each beam enjoys the full gain of the aperture. Further, the moderate BFN loss is inconsequential since the beam forming is done before the power amplifiers on Tx and after the low noise amplifiers on Rx. As a result, high gain overlapping beams can be produced with this approach.

articleTitle: A CPW electromagnetically fed slot antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed slot antennas are attractive due to fabrication simplicity and ease of integration with active devices. Typically the feeder is directly connected to the slot and the equivalent radiation impedance cannot be tuned easily. In this communication a new concept for exciting slots with a CPW line is presented. It is described how this coupling structure can he designed to tune the impedance of the antenna over a wide range. Three antennas built for 5 GHz operation are described. Simulated and measured characteristics are presented.

articleTitle: Determining microstrip antenna input impedance using standard circuit CAD programs
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip antennas have been widely used during the past four decades due to mechanical and economical advantages. The rigorous analysis of the microstrip antenna involves the solution of an electric field integral equation (EFIE) whose kernel must account for the effect of the dielectric slab. In this paper a simple approach for determining input impedance and resonant frequencies of microstrip antennas is given. Arbitrary shaped microstrip antenna can be divided using TLM (Transmission Line Modelling) approach into an integer number of square and half square (triangle) subsections. Every subsection can be replaced with crossed transmission lines, i.e. with their lumped element model. There are four types of subsections: inner, outer, corner, and diagonal [1]. Inner subsection shows nondispersive parallel plate behaviour. The outer subsection model requires effective dielectric calculation and is frequency dependent. Models for corner and diagonal subsections are obtained using inner and outer section models. For microstrip antennas analysis model given in [1] have been improved concerning conductor loses, and substrate loses are involved, too. In this way it is possible to consider simple electrical circuit instead of considering complex electromagnetic structure. Such circuit can be clumsy a lot, but it can be solved using standard CAD programs. A few years ago there were problems with regard to number of nodes and the largeness of the circuit file. Nowadays, those limitations are practically declined and this admission is actual. The appropriate interface program is realised for automated circuit file generation.

articleTitle: A Ka-band HBT four-stage low noise amplifier
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A Ka-band GaInP/GaAs HBT four-stage LNA has been designed and fabricated. This circuit is to be used in a multifunction T/R module for local multipoint distribution systems (LMDS) which include both analog and digital transmission. An average noise figure of 6 dB from 27 GHz to 30 GHz, and a gain of greater than 15 dB were measured. These results are the best reported at Ka-band for a LNA using transistors from digital HBT library.

articleTitle: Focal field concentration in interstitial hyperthermia with an array of linear polarization radiators
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Until now, the problem of interstitial hyperthermia was solved as a forward problem. When a circular array of radiators is concerned, symmetrical SAR curves were obtained for equal antenna currents; and some authors changed the phases of the antenna currents as an arithmatical sequence and observed some changes of the patterns. In this paper, the inverse problem is solved. With a proper election of the phases and amplitudes of antenna currents, focal field concentration at certaion target points are obtained. If these target points are chosen closely in a certain region, then this region gets higher SAR values when compared to the case of equal currents. It is found that for the operating frequency 2.45 GHz, higher increments in SAR can be obtained. This incerement can be 13.84 dB for a single target point; and 11.14 dB for two target points chosen 1.128 cm apart. Similar results with less increments are obtained for 915 MHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of microstrip antennas integrated with feed networks
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It has often been claimed that the microstrip antenna can be easily integrated with the feed network and circuitry on the same substrate. However, if this is actually done some compromise must be made between a good antenna performance and an acceptable circuit behavior [1]. The root of this problem lies in the fact that antenna radiation and circuitry are distinct electrical functions. Antennas require loosely bound fields for radiation into space, hence suggests the use of an electrically thick substrate with low ∊<inf>r</inf>. On the other hand a microwave circuit requires tightly bound fields to prevent undesired radiation or coupling, suggesting the use of dectrically thin, high ∊<inf>r</inf> substrates, which in turn degrades the antenna performance.

articleTitle: Effect of radome on mutual coupling of finite array of circular waveguides and cavities
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The electrical characteristics of planar arrays are dependent on the mutual coupling of elements in the array. The degree of coupling depends on the element type, scan angle, array geometry, excitation and polarization of each element. The analysis therefore should include all these factors for better modeling and design of an array.

articleTitle: A novel design of a shaped reflector for the intelsat viii-a program
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Consistent with plans to provide global satellite interconnectivity [1], INTELSAT authorized construction of two additional satellites known as 805 and 806. The 805 satellite provides Asia-Pacific service with an enhanced coverage over China as viewed from the 1.10.5° East orbital location while the 806 coverage includes North/South America and Western Europe as viewed from the 310° East orbital location. The design of the antenna subsystem for these satellites is driven by several unique requirements including in-orbit polarization selectivity with stringent cross-pol isolation, high edge of coverage EIRP (which drives power handling requirements) and extended bandwidth operation which complicates the design of the components. The in-orbit polarization selectability permits either dual linear or dual circular polarization, both with frequency reuse. The in-orbit 26 dB cross-pol isolation requirement imposes stringent cross-polar constraints on all four polarizations. This requirement is necessary since standard Intelsat ground stations operate with circular polarization while other current systems servicing these markets use linear polarization. At the initiation of the contract, uncertainties in the coordination of these different systems led to this dual polarization requirement [2].

articleTitle: Complex near-field antenna measurements using infrared (IR) thermograms
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes the application of the plane-to-plane (PTP) iterative Fourier processing technique to infrared thermographic images of microwave fields to calculate the near-field and farfield patterns of radiating antennas. A resistive sheet is positioned in a radiating field, and a thermal picture is then taken of the heat pattern. Each pixel of this thermal image represents a measurement of the intensity (magnitude) of the field at the pixel location on the resistive sheet. The PTP technique allows recovery of the phase by combining measurements made on two planes, both in the radiating near field of the antenna under test. Starting with an estimate of the phase and the measured magnitudes, Fourier processing techniques are used to iteratively propagate between the planes to determine the correct phase distribution at each plane. We describe the technique and show comparisons made between the predicted results and results from measured IR thermograms of the field of a 36 element patch array antenna operating at 4 GHz using the University of Colorado, Colorado Springs (UCCS) Thermal Camera.

articleTitle: Antennas for the lstar satellite
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The government of Laos with a group of private investors, called Asia Broadcasting and Communication Network Company Limited (ABCN), have purchased two satellites from Space Systems/Loral to provide satellite communications that will include direct to home (DTH) TV broadcast and VSAT across Asia Pacific. The satellites, LSTAR-1 and LSTAR-2, will be the most powerful satellites to be launched for DTH service in the region. Each satellite will be capable of transmitting as many as 200 digitally compressed video channels to users in the region, using terminals smaller than 50 cm. The first satellite LSTAR-1, will commence service in the winter of 1998 and LSTAR-2, the second satellite, will be in service in 1999. The antenna design for the LSTAR communication satellite uses all shaped Gregorian antenna designs. This provides the highest possible copolarization efficiency and the lowest cross polarization characteristics for this application. This paper will discuss the design criterion for the three coverage beams of this satellite, and will show the predicted performance for each antenna. The three coverages will be isolated from each other to implement frequency reuse by virtue of spatial diversity, and within each coverage, polarization isolation will be maintained to allow frequency reuse by polarization diversity. The design considerations to accommodate these features will be discussed. A discussion will be included of the shaped Gregorian antenna design and the applications for which it is best suited. Since the three coverage beams for this satellite will operate the downlink and uplink bands simultaneously in each oí the three antennas, design considerations to avoid undesirable Passive InterModulation (PIM) products will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Stepped helical antenna modeling using “nec” and validation by measurements
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper investigates the validation of a modeling software for helical antennas. One of the benefits of the stepped helical antenna, which consists of two or more cylindrical helices of different diameters, is its capability, under some conditions, of providing a large bandwidth. It is also simpler and cheaper than a tapered helix. For spacecraft applications, a theoretical design of such an antenna can allow the flexibility for optimization of the antenna size and weight. This paper presents an analysis and modeling of stepped helical antennas. It provides theoretical performance prediction. Corresponding helices were built and tested to validate the theoretical prediction. The experimental performances are in good agreement with the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Broadband MIC 4-bit phase shifter to control a phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes the design of a low cost 4-bit switched line phase shifter microwave integrated circuit (MIC) on a 10 mil Alumina substrate. Schiffman coupled lines were used to implement each of the 4 bits. These coupled lines provide a dispersive phase response which can be used to produce a relatively constant phase shift over a large bandwidth. Over the 4–8 GHz frequency range, initial measurements have shown that the bandwidth requirement was met. The dimensions of the 4-bit phase shifter are 5.5 cm × 1.0 cm.
