articleTitle: An analytic method for dealing with ionosphere propagation
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An analytic method is developed to calculate the reflection and transmission of electromagnetic waves as they propagate through the ionosphere region. The model chosen for this study is a magnetized, steady-state, two-dimensional, nonuniform plasma region, which is presented by a number of parallel flat layers. The fields in each layer are written in the form of summation of the appropriate eigen functions weighted by unknown scattering coefficients. These coefficients are determined via the application of the boundary conditions at each interface. Successive application of the boundary conditions results in obtaining a matrix of scattering coefficients. This method hereafter is referred to as the Scattering Matrix Model (SMM). Presentative numerical results for reflected and transmitted powers of the electromagnetic waves through the ionosphere are presented.

articleTitle: Radio channel simulation for micro-cellular wireless personal communication systems
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Radio channel models developed for traditional macro-cellular systems can not be used for micro- and pico-cellular environments of modern wireless personal communication systems (PCS). This is mainly because of distinct differences in propagation characteristics and much smaller outdoor and indoor micro-cell sizes [1]. It is therefore essential to develop site specific models [2], [3] for a realistic simulation of radio channel and its temporal and spectral characterizations.

articleTitle: HBT oscillator employing a slot coupled sapphire resonator to achieve low phase noise performance
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) MIC oscillator stabilized by a novel slot coupled sapphire resonator (SCSR) is reported. Common base mode device operation is utilized, transistor destabilization being achieved via series inductive feedback between base and ground. The SCSR, which has an unloaded Q-factor of 2500, is reaction coupled to the emitter circuit of the HBT to facilitate frequency stabilization. Single sideband (ssb) phase noise performance for the topology of −58dBc/Hz and −92dBc/Hz has been achieved at offset frequencies of 1KHz and 10KHz respectively from the oscillator carrier frequency of 6.40GHz.

articleTitle: A self-consistent formalism of absorbing boundary condition for modeling unbounded electromagnetic structures
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A simple approach is proposed to construct a class of absorbing boundary conditions which is suitable for modeling completely or partially unbounded electromagnetic structures under finite-element and/or finite-difference frameworks. These self-consistent absorbing boundary conditions are derived and obtained by applying the method of lines with various coordinate systems, which are formulated in terms of analytical matrix equations. Potential application of the absorbing boundary conditions may be found in frequency domain as well as in rime domain with interesting features related to mesh truncation, modeling of radiation, scattering and propagation problems. Demonstrative result is presented for a simple one-dimensional geometry.

articleTitle: A new optical technique for feeding microwave microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In the literature, several techniques have been presented for feeding microstrip antennas with RF-modulated lightwave signals via optical fiber. This paper describes a new technique, the novelty of which is that it uses integrated optical waveguides as the main feed network of the electrooptic antennas. We use the basic spectral domain method to analyze the antennas and we compute the overlap fields integral to point out lightwave and microwave electrooptic interaction.

articleTitle: Multiple beam antenna arrays for indoor communications
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A practical design of a multiple beam antenna array for indoor wireless communications is presented. This antenna is formed using a linear array of equally spaced elements, fed with an improved printed circuit Rotman lens. Both the lens and the array are designed and built on the same dielectric substrate. The antenna operates in frequency range of 27–30 GHz and covers an angular sector near 120 degrees with more than 10 beams. A full azimuth coverage can be obtained through a set of three antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical investigation of a microstrip to NRD transition
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Transitions between microstrip and NRD-guide are required by integrating NRD circuits to planar circuits and NRD circuit measurement. The transition proposed in [1] offers a promising solution in view of practical applications, but it has to be accurately modeled and optimized to achieve its best possible performance. In this paper, the transmission line matrix (TLM) method has been successfully used in the simulation of such a transition. It is found that theoretical results are in good agreement with experiments. This may provide an alternative way to field-theoretically design this structure at desired microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: A single-arm spiral antenna with a tilted beam
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A circularly polarized wave (CPW) radiation beam tilted from the direction normal to an antenna plane can be obtained using a spiral antenna [1]. The authors have numerically analyzed this type of spiral antenna [2], [3]. In Reference [2], the center of a two-arm spiral antenna is shifted towards the outer circumference, while in Reference [3] a single-arm spiral antenna is used without shifting the spiral center.

articleTitle: Large signal activities at ENST paris
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Load-Pull measurements are essential to characterize power devices accurately. This paper presents recent and current load-pull measurement systems and projects at ENST Paris. The activities presented here cover comparative measurements of a 1 W high power transistor and the development of a multiharmonic load-pull system based on the sixport technique, including new solutions for control software and on-wafer calibration.

articleTitle: A Ka-band circularly polarized dielectric resonator modelled using the transmission-line-matrix method
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna has been developed recently for K-Band applications [1]. A microstrip aperture-coupled dielectric resonator element in the shape of a cross was designed as a feed element for a cylindrical cavity antenna. The analysis was performed using a Finite Difference Time Domain (FD-TD) method [2]. As part of the continuing development of this antenna, it is being modelled at higher frequencies using a Transmission-Line-Matrix (TLM) method detailed in [3]. The TLM method is a differential-equation based numerical analysis technique, which is capable of determining approximate solutions of the time-dependent Maxwell's equations in the presence of complex environments. It is especially suited to the non-planar, non-homogeneous aperture-fed geometry of the antenna under consideration. This paper presents the results obtained from the TLM simulation of the aperture-fed dielectric cross, both as an individual element and as the feed element for the cylindrical cavity. Theoretical results are compared to the experimental results for the complete cavity geometry. This theoretical approach allows for optimization of the antenna element without the necessity of performing several measurements.

articleTitle: Modeling of interactions of cellular telephones with the user and implantable medical devices
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: With the expansion of current use and anticipated further increases in the use of cellular telephones and other personal communication services (PCS), there has been an interest and considerable research effort devoted to interactions between antennas on handsets and the human body. These activities are motivated by two factors: (i) a need to evaluate deterioration of the antenna performance and to develop better antennas, and (ii) a need to evaluate the rates of RF energy deposition, called specific absorption rates (SAR), in order to evaluate potential health effects and compliance with standards. There is also a concern regarding electromagnetic interference (EMI) by PCS with critical care medical devices, particularly those implantable.

articleTitle: EMC engineering of small communications systems using a cispr absorbing clamp
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes how the Comité International Spécial des Perturbations, Radioélectriques (CISPR) Absorbing Clamp can be used in design testing to optimize radiated emissions from small systems, whose physical size is small in comparison with a wavelength, and the electromagnetic interference is radiated mostly by the cables. The Absorbing Clamp is a simple, repeatable test which requires less investment in time and cost than Open Field Site testing, which is the main alternative. During an engineering phase of the product development stage, repeated testing is done to assess the impact of design modifications on system performance. Successful use of the Absorbing Clamp during product development, to evaluate the impact of design modifications on system radiated electromagnetic emissions, is demonstrated. Test results confirm that the Absorbing Clamp is a repeatable and inexpensive test method for EMC engineering on small systems.

articleTitle: A study on some features of the solution of general bianisotropic waveguides
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The calculation of general bianisotropic waveguides are often quite complicated. In the procedures of these solutions, complicated expressions should be handled and their interpretation becomes difficult. In this presentation, we shall deduct rigorous and general equations for the field components in matrix form which is quite simple, easy to be incorporated into computer software and important features of bianisotropic waveguides can be obtained. The solutions of bianisotropic circular and parallel-plate waveguides will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization of high-speed VLSI interconnects
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: With the rapid increase in operating frequency in today's electronic systems such as computers and digital communication systems, VLSI interconnects become one of the critical issues in an overall system design, in recent years, research into the interconnect optimization problem has been very active, and several important progresses have been made. Recent advances in signal integrity oriented optimization of interconnects at different levels of electronics systems, are reviewed together with various optimization techniques with highlights on the large scale optimization oriented techniques. Macromodeling techniques and advanced formulations of interconnect optimizations featuring manufacturability oriented and multidisciplinary design objectives are also discussed.

articleTitle: Validation of computed portable radio handset near fields by measurement
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper compares the measured and computed fields of a portable radio at 850 MHz operated adjacent to a simple representation of the head, either a box or a sphere. The measurement uses an aluminum box for a handset, with a quarter-wave monopole antenna. The box or sphere representing the head is a thin plexiglas shell filled with liquid having the electrical properties of the human brain. The measurement setup uses a near field scanner to measure the vertical component of the electric field over planes 50 by 50 cm in size. The computation uses the finite-difference time-domain method, with a sinusoidal generator at the base of the monopole and time-stepping to steady-state. Comparing measured and computed contour maps of E<inf>z</inf> shows good agreement for the handset alone, with “hot spots” at the base of the case, at the top of the case near the antenna feed point, and at the tip of the antenna. When the box or sphere “head” is present, reasonable agreement is obtained, and the “hot spots” remain.

articleTitle: EMI sources and modeling techniques
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The prediction of EMI sources in electrical and digital devices is not a simple task. In practice it is difficult to predict all the possible sources of EMI, from even relatively simple devices. This paper reviews and summarizes the possible EMI sources and the numerical electromagnetic modeling techniques that can be used to analyze these sources of electromagnetic interference. Although there are many different possible modeling problems. most of which can be broken down into specific classes. Four different modeling problems are presented here as representative of EMI modeling in general. It is hoped that these problems will help engineers to understand how to reduce the overall EMI problem into elements that can be effectively modeled, and so better understand and evaluate alternative modeling approaches and tools.

articleTitle: Efficient full-wave CAD of waveguide diplexers
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper presents an efficient CAD algorithm for the design of waveguide front-end diplexers. Three different types of junctions can be employed: E-plane T-junction, H-plane T-junction and E-plane bifurcation. Channel filter configurations currently include — but are not limited to — waveguide stub filters and inductive-iris filters. The diplexer design is performed in three basic steps: synthesis, analysis and optimization. In order to improve the computing efficiency of the design algorithm, highly accurate transmission line models are used in the initial component design and optimization stages. The final optimization and the analysis of the entire diplexer makes use of a full-wave mode-matching model, which can include waveguide transformers at all ports. The CAD routine is verified against measurments, and excellent agreement between predicted and measured results is obtained.

articleTitle: Application of the real frequency method to the design of microwave amplifier and laser command circuit for remote antenna link
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Up until now the simplified real frequency technique has been applied to the design of broadband multistage microwave amplifiers where gain and VSWR are optimized. In this paper we extend the method to the optimization of noise figure in parallel with gain and VSWR. Another extension of the method concern the design of broadband laser comnmand circuit for remote antenna link. The specifics characteristics of this circuit are optimized.

articleTitle: Short pulse backscattering measurements on conducting cylindrical cavities
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Re-entrant cavities on modem jet aircrafts like the engine intakes, the exhaust ducts and the cockpit are usually considered as main contributors to the global RCS of the target and as wide FOV scattering centers. Though the scattering of a cavity has been studied theoretically by many authors, most of the studies have been particularly focused on the frequency domain, whereas few experimental data are until now available in the time-domain. The present paper reports recent measurements of impulse scattering on cylindrical cavities carried out directly in the time-domain with the Time-Domain Scattering Range of the Royal Military Academy (RMA) Brussels. The monostatic impulse responses of a conducting cylinder open at one end and shorted at the other end are measured with a gaussian plane wave excitations having a pulsewidth of 90 ps and 320 ps. One of the measured responses is also compared with the transient response of the cavity calculated by FDTD. Because the high spatial resolution obtained with excitation pulses as short as 90 ps, the various physical phenomena involved in the plane wave scattering of a cavity like edge diffraction and bottom reflection can be separed in time. Hence the analysis of the impulse responses give insight into the various mechanisms contributing to the global RCS of a cavity.

articleTitle: CFH Simulation for high speed VLSI interconnects with 3D full wave model
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, we present a new method for the analysis of high speed VLSI interconnect networks, which combines the advantages of CFH circuit level simulation technique and the full wave FDTD analyisis. First, the overall interconnect network is divided into many substructures whose behaviours can be represented by full wave macromodels. Secondly, the full wave macromodel is formulated into the overall network equation which includes many transmission lines and lumped elements. Finally, The CFH method is used to handle the full wave case. Compared with FDTD analysis for the overall circuit, the stability required for our method is easier to be satisfied, and less CPU time is needed. Several networks including single, coupled, bend transmission lines are used to verify the efficiency and accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Rf design concept of a wide-band L-band SAR spacecraft antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: At L-band the most practical implementation of space borne SAR antennas requires the use of microstrip radiating elements. However, printed antennas are usually characterized by inherently narrow bandwidth which limits the range resolution capability of the system. In order to develop an L-band SAR antenna design with enhanced bandwidth performance Spar and CAL have performed studies aimed at 5% (1.5 VSWR) bandwidth. Other design drivers have included low mass, high gain, good sidelobe control and low cross-polarization. The results of these studies are presented here as a conceptual design for an L-band SAR antenna which is able to meet typical requirements derived from data user needs.

articleTitle: Optical waveguides for coherent optical control of phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In coherent optical architectures for phased array antennas, the frequency and phase of the microwave carrier at each element are determined by optical heterodyning two laser signals of differing frequency. Semiconductor diode lasers can be frequency-stabilized with sufficient precision so that their difference frequency can serve as a stable microwave carrier.<sup>1</sup> Another approach is to divide a single laser beam into two paths and frequency shift one of them using acoustooptic or electrooptic devices. For a phased array, both laser signals must be distributed among a large number of photodetectors. one for each antenna element. The optical signal distribution can use free-optics, as in the Fourier optics scheme first proposed by Koepf,<sup>4</sup> or it can make use of integrated optical devices<sup>2</sup> in which power splitting, phase shifting, and power recombining all take place in a single solid state device. The principle advantage of the latter is that, unlike free-space optical systems, the path delays can easily be controlled and stabilized to the required sub-micron tolerances.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic plane wave by conducting convex plate
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Scattering problems of electromagnetic plane wave by conducting plate of arbitrary shape are studied nsing physical theory of diffraction (PTD). PTD solution consists of physical optic (PO) solution and its correction due to nonuniform edge current. Usually PO solution is given by surface integral with integrand which includes the amplitude multiplied by linear phase term. When this amplitude is constant, the PO radiation integral can be transformed into contour integral using Stokes's theorem which has been developed by Gordon <sup>[1]</sup>. This contour integral may be performed analytically for special cases of triangular, rectangular, circular and elliptic conducting disks, but we have to rely on numerical integration for general disks. For convex plate, an asymptotic solution for the contour integral is derived using the stationary phase method of integration. There are two stationary points in this integrand which correspond to diffraction points and the solution has a simple physical interpretation that diffracted field comes from these two diffraction points <sup>[2]</sup>. The amplitudes of the diffracted rays are found to be proportional to the square root of the radius of curvature at the diffraction point. Using the similarity of the derived asymptotic solution with that of circular disk which is obtained by applying asymptotic expansion to the Airy pattern, we deduce the caustic corrected solution <sup>[3]</sup>. The validity of the expression is verified numerically for special shaped convex plate. Next, the expression for the non-unifourm edge correction is derived by applying the equivalent current method (ECM) to Ufimtsev's edge current <sup>[4],[5]</sup>. For convex plate, the asymptotic expression is derived usiug the stationary phase method of integration. For special case of circular disk the PTD solution agrees completely with that obtained by Ufimtsev <sup>[3]</sup>.

articleTitle: A least square method for optimization of thinned antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper concerns a least square approach to optimizing a thinned antenna array with respect to antenna spacing to improve the sidelobe performance. A least square method based on a modified version of the perturbation method is proposed to efficiently synthesize an optimum pattern in a thinned array. It is demonstrated that the array performance improves with the proposed method.

articleTitle: Efficient techniques for choosing the regularization parameter for microwave imaging
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The usual procedure for the microwave imaging in spatial domain consists in discretizing the electric field integral equations in the form of two coupled matrix equations by applying the moment method[l]-[8]. The associated ill-conditioned systems of algebraic equations are solved iteratively by implementing a regularization technique at each iteration step. One of the difficulties in the procedure is the selection of the regularization parameter[1]-[8]. If this parameter is too big, too much useful information could be lost. If it is too small, a convergent solution might not be obtained. Based on the stochastic inversion algorithm, this paper presents three methods for the selection of this parameter. The first method is applicable to the situation when the upper bound of the object function variance and the upper bound of the measured data noise variance are known. The second method can be used if only the upper bound of the object function variance is detectable. If this information is not available, the third method can be employed to find the regularization parameter. The efficiency of these methods is illustrated by reconstructing two-dimensional dielectric objects with noiseless measured data and also with data containing noise.

articleTitle: Development of a gimballed, dual frequency, satellite microwave antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A two-axis gimballed dual-frequency antenna has been developed for use on a commercial communications satellite. Figure 1 is a general layout of this antenna. Four antennas per satellite are to be used for up and downlink communications with Earth-based stations located anywhere within each satellite's field of view. The following table summarizes the key performance requirements for these antennas and the results obtained from early production model testing.

articleTitle: 60 GHz simple, short range communication system test
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In intelligent vehicle and highway systems, intelligent vehicles must have communication equipment and radar sensors. The communication equipment is used to communicate with other vehicles or road-side base stations, and the radar sensors detect preceding vehicles on the road. Therefore, to be widely used in the future, this equipment must be economical. For economical equipment to become a reality in intelligent systems, a 60GHz simple, short-range system for vehicle communication is proposed. This equipment can be constructed using radar sensor equipment which can be used for both measuring distance to a preceding vehicle, and for communication to the same vehicle. This paper describes the 60GHz communication system for use in an intelligent vehicle and its test results.

articleTitle: Analysis of discontinuities in inhomogeneously doped slow-wave coplanar waveguide using the FDTLM method
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper present a numerical investigation of discontinuities between coplanar waveguide (CPW) and slow-wave MIS CPW with inhomogeneous doping regions. The frequency-domain TLM (FDTLM) method is applied to calculate the scattering parameters for the abrupt transition from a normal CPW on insulating substrate to an MIS CPW on doped substrate. The effect of various lateral widths of the doping region on the S-parameters of such a transition is investigated. It is found that limiting the lateral extend of the doping region to the area below the slots and the center conductor not only provides a high slow-wave factor at low losses but also provides much better S-parameters compared to the case where the doping is extended over the whole transmission line cross-section.

articleTitle: Multi-Stack Quantum Barrier varactor frequency tripiers, an efficient way for mm-wave power generation
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Constantly growing market of commercial mm-wave applications such as Indoor Wireless Links, Automotive Radars etc., require the development of new efficient and cost effective integrated power sources. Frequency multipliers based on Schottky diodes and FET transistors have dominated this field of application. However, the necessity of bias and Idlers circuits in the above mentioned multipliers make them difficult to realise especially at mm-waves. A new class of symmetrical characteristics diodes such as the Multi-Stack Quantum Barrier Varactor (MSQBV) require no bias nor idlers and generate only odd harmonics of the input frequency. This make them very attractive for applications as mm-wave frequency tripiers. The MSQBV is a hetero-structure GaAs/InP composite material. The barrier region is made of high band gap materials and is sandwiched between two lightly doped regions. The contacts at the top and bottom of the device are of Ohmic type. The whole structure acts as a variable capacitance with symmetrical response around zero bias voltage. In this paper, recent results in the development of MSQBV based frequency tripiers at mm-wave are presented.

articleTitle: EHF active integrated arrays designed for device integration
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A conventional transmit system design comprises a high gain antenna followed by a solid state power amplifier (SSPA). However, the SSPA used within a transmit system have in general multiple devices to provide the high output power and suffers from the combining losses within the unit. To reduce these losses, low to medium power amplifiers are integrated within an array architecture. Spatial power combining is employed thus the path loss from the amplifier to radiating element within the array is the only source of combining loss. It is therefore preferred to locate amplifiers as close as possible to the radiating elements. This is essential when developing array architectures at EHF where a microstrip feed network is utilized. The resistive losses increase rapidly with frequency hence the path loss from amplifier to radiating element could be severe. In addition, the structural aspects of the array must be such to accommodate device integration near the radiating elements.

articleTitle: Radar cross section analysis of major scatterers
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It is of great tactical significance to determine the radar cross sections (RCS) of the major scattering centres on naval ships. To assist naval engineers in the ranking of ship reflectors for RAM treatment, MATLAB software was developed. RCS profiles of flat plates, dihedrals and trihedrals were calculated using the theory of physical optics, the method of equivalent currents, geometric optics and ray tracing techniques. The RCS profiles obtained are in excellent agreement with other theoretical models in the literature [1-3], as well as with actual experimental measurements [3]. The program developed allows for frequency and viewing elevation control, which is of great practical interest from a ship defence perspective.

articleTitle: Investigation of dielectric resonator antennas for L-band communications
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An investigation of rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antennas (DRA) for use in mobile communications applications was undertaken at L-Band frequencies (1–2 GHz). Techniques were developed to improve the performance of probe fed DRA. The resonant frequency was reduced by 40% by grounding the edge of the DRA opposite the feed probe. Inserting a low dielectric constant material between the DRA and the ground plane increased the impedance bandwidth by 84%. A four element array of DRA has been developed which uses three of the DRA as parasitic elements to tilt a dual polarized radiation pattern by 45° from broadside towards the horizon. At an angle of 20° in elevation the difference in E and H-plane magnitudes was reduced from 7.5 dB for a single element to 2.5 dB for the parasitic array.

articleTitle: Imagerie thermique par radiometrie microonde en champ proche
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: La radiométrie microonde est une technique capable de détecter l'existence de gradients thermiques au sein d'un milieu dissipatif par la mesure de bruit électromagnétique émis naturellement par le milieu. Il en résulte des procédés thermométriques passifs intéressant les applications médicales [1], industrielles [2] et plus récemment la domotique [3].

articleTitle: Reciprocal circular polarization selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the concept of an electromagnetic surface called the Circular Polarization Selective Surface (CPSS). Few papers have dealt with the CPSS and it has even been argued that the ideal CPSS belongs to the category of impossible polarizers. We present herein a theoretical proof for the existence of the ideal CPSS, review the prior art in this area, identify some geometrical constraints inherent to such a device and present the results of numerical computations.

articleTitle: Validation of a scalar potential finite-difference code for extremely low frequency magnetic induction modelling using an analytical method
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of numerical and analytical calculations of the low-frequency electric and current density fields, induced by an applied uniform axial magnetic field, in an equatorially stratified sphere having the conductivity distribution σ(ϕ) = σ<inf>0</inf>e<sup>−λ cos (pϕ)</sup> with p ∊ {1, 2} and λ > 0.

articleTitle: Analysis of a rectangular microstrip patch on biaxial dielectric substrates
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the analysis and simulation of a rectangular microstrip patch antenna on a single or two dielectric anisotropic substrates. The anisotropy under study is biaxial and the dielectric tensor may have nondiagonal elements which represent misalignment, on the surface, between the material coordinate system and the patch coordinate system. Among the great number of works carried out on microstrip antennas, few have taken the anisotropy of the substrates into account. Neglecting this anisotropy may cause important errors on antenna simulations.

articleTitle: An efficient algorithm for the calculation of transient radiated fields from printed circuit interconnects
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Simulation of the electromagnetic fields radiated from high speed printed circuits is becoming increasingly important in system design as well as to ensure compliance with present electromagnetic compatibility standards. In this paper electromagnetic radiation due to high speed signals on printed circuit board, multi-chip module, and integrated circuit interconnects is examined using a simple closed form solution for the time domain radiated fields due to an arbitrary interconnect geometry. The developed technique is intended to use currents generated by common, time domain, circuit simulation softwares to calculate the desired transient fields. The accuracy of the method is addressed and one example involving transmission line mismatches and ringing is given.

articleTitle: Integrated lna/antennas for 30 GHz receivers
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes the modeling, design and performance of 30 GHz low noise amplifiers (LNAs) integrated with slot antennas on GaAs monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs). Various designs are compared, showing the tradeoffs between achievable noise figure, gain and overall chip size.

articleTitle: Gii overview and the roles of satellites in the GII (Invited paper)
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This presentation will give an overview of the vision for the Global Information Infrastructure (GII). The concept of the GII as a worldwide “network of networks” that will create a global information marketplace, encouraging broadbased social discourse within and among all countries, will be presented. The GII is creating an information explosion that is producing ever increasing demands on all communications systems. Satellites will be an essential element of the GII, providing services and capabilities never available before. The presentation will discuss the roles and challenges for satellite systems to operate seamlessly with terrestrial networks and be fully included in the GII.

articleTitle: A modification to berenger's PML equations for FDTD method
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper. Berenger's twelve split-formtime-domain-PML equations have been reduced to only six unsplit-form equations by rearranging the constitutive parameters of the PML region. The modified PML equations have two advantages, viz., a) computer time and memory savings and, b) ease of implementation. The disadvantage is that the interface between free space and PML region is no longer perfectly reflectionless. Methods for reducing this effect are suggested. Numerical results show that the accuracy of the modified PML equations can be very close to that of the original PML equations.

articleTitle: Human presence effects on the wireless SHF/EHF channel
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Channel variations due to movement of people in the indoor propagation environment are expected to be particularly significant in the SHF/EHF bands. This paper reports CW measurements performed at 30.1 GHz between two fixed terminals in a single room to determine the amplitude and speed of temporal variations of the envelope when individuals are moving in the environment. In particular, it is shown that the importance of fluctuations is dependent not only on the degree of movement but also on the spatial fading situation when the room is empty.

articleTitle: Correlating numerical and scale modelled experimental radiation characteristics of a ship-mounted high frequency antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation characteristics of high frequency (HF) wire antennas mounted on ships are affected by the irregularly shaped conducting ship structure. Computer codes based on the moment method (MM) and the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) can compute the radiation pattern of a wire antenna over a simplified model ship composed of a limited number of plates. Such computations do not consider high orders of multiple reflections and/or diffractions. A scale model ship could be built to resemble an actual ship and placed inside an anechoic chamber on a finite size ground plane. In this work, the radiation patterns of a vertical quarter-wave monopole mounted at different positions on top of a ship scale model were measured inside C-CORE's anechoic chamber and correlated with those patterns calculated for the simplified ship model using MM and GTD methods. A good agreement is observed between measured and calculated patterns. This work supports computer codes which are used to determine quantitatively the considerable impact of irregular ship structures on the radiation patterns of onboard antennas.

articleTitle: The historic development of spaceborne SAR antenna in Canada
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The use of synthetic aperture radar on aircraft became well established in the first half of the seventies. It has enabled much better resolution to be obtained than that achievable with conventional radar. A conventional side looking imaging radar achieves range resolution by employing short RF pulses and azimuth resolution by means of a narrow antenna beamwidth. To create a narrow beamwidth with a physical aperture requires an antenna many wavelengths long. Due to the difficulty of building large airborne antennas, conventional side looking radars were generally restricted to low altitude aircraft and were operated at high microwave frequencies (10–30GHz).

articleTitle: A planar diversity antenna for hand-held PCS devices
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The performance of a diversity antenna and a monopole antenna on a hand-held PCS device are compared, and the presence of the body (head and hand) is considered. Two versions of the diversity antenna result in less power absorbed in the head than when the monopole is used, but the power absorbed in the hand is higher. For all three antennas, the hand does not significantly alter the shape of the radiation pattern of the dominant polarization, but it absorbs a substantial amount of power, causing the total polarization angle to deviate from the ideal. The head distorts the shape of the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: PHEMT MMIC switch for 30 GHz communications systems
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A monolithic GaAs Ka-band rf control switch has been developed for use in wireless communications systems. The switch consists of two parallel-resonated GaAs PHEMTs in a shunt single-pole double-throw (SPDT) configuration and has very low dc power dissipation, 1.0 dB insertion loss, and 35 dB isolation. A simple small-signal model is presented to explain the basic features of a resonated PHEMT switch. The switch has a robust design and is adaptable to numerous rf control applications such as phase shifters, transmit inhibit circuits, and broadband wireless LAN systems (WLAN).

articleTitle: Efficient modeling and simulation of interconnects
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An efficient method to compute the 2-D capacitance matrix of coupled microstrip lines is presented. The method is also applicable to conductors of arbitrary polygon shape embedded in a multilayered dielectric medium with possible ground planes on the top or bottom of the dielectric layers. An optimal technique for the transient simulation of distributed multiconductor RLGC lines is then used by applying an indirect numerical integration scheme to the device model for a distributed line. The resulting technique can be directly used in a circuit simulator. The computational complexity is linearly proportional to the number of time steps.

articleTitle: Characteristics of printed ring microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip ring antennas are investigated numerically and experimentally. Depending on their selected geometry, they provide additional parameters that can be used to control their resonant frequency and impedance. Methods for improving their bandwidth and cross-polarization are also investigated.

articleTitle: Analysis of slotted microstrip — A simple line with vast range of characteristic impedance
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The asymptotic behavior of the characteristic impedance (Z<inf>0</inf>) of a slotted microstripline is used to develop a very simple and accurate approximate formula for Z<inf>0</inf>. A method of moments (MoM) analysis of the structure is used to verify the formula's accuracy. The use of a 2-D quasi-static complex images Green's function in MoM allows fast and accurate computation of the characteristic impedance Z<inf>0</inf>. It is shown that a wide range of Z<inf>0</inf> can be achieved by varying the slot width to the strip width ratio (s/w). This makes the line suitable for matching ordinary 50Ω feed lines to the very low input impedance of for instance most superconducting devices.

articleTitle: Numerically efficient fullwave analysis of inhornogeneously-loaded top hat monopole
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of a top hat monopole antenna loaded with an inhomogeneous dielectric is analyzed using mode matching techniques. The inhomogeneous dielectric loading takes the form of two radial layers of dielectric underneath the top hat, the innermost of which may be made up of two vertically-stacked dielectric layers. A very general numerical code has been developed and used to compute the input impedance, radiation quality factor, and radiation efficiency of several electrically-small, loaded top hat monopoles. The results are checked for self-consistency by computing input impedance from driving current and voltage as well as from near field energy and radiated power.

articleTitle: Modeling, analysis, designing and realization of MMDS corner reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper a procedure for the synthesis of the receiving MMDS corner reflector antenna is given. The antenna was modeled and its performances have been analysed as functions of the antenna parameters. Optimisation criteria were based on the specific area of the comer reflector antenna implementation. It has been shown that synthesised antenna satisfies given requirements. Optimal antenna was designed and realized. Measured and calculated results were compared.

articleTitle: A novel circular polarization selective surface made of resonant helices
publicationTitle: 1996 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A Circular Polarization Selective Surface (CPSS) is an electromagnetic surface that reflects one sense of a circularly polarized (CP) wave but is transparent to the other sense. In this paper, a new CPSS with improved characteristics is presented. This new CPSS is made of special square helices. Because the helices can be supported at their extremities, this CPSS does not need a dielectric support as other CPSSs do and therefore can be made more transparent. The response of the CPSS to a plane wave excitation was simulated using the method of moments for thin wires. Mutual coupling and losses were taken into account. Simulation results show that the radar cross-section of the surface to one circular polarization sense is 50 times higher than to the other polarization sense. A CPSS has been fabricated and measurements showed good agreement with the theory.
